title: Using a web browser
content: A browser is an application for opening websites. Type a website address into the address bar and press Enter. Use the Back button to return to the previous page. A tab lets you keep more than one page open.

title: አሳሽ መጠቀም
content: አሳሽ ድረ ገጾችን ለመክፈት የሚያገለግል መተግበሪያ ነው። የድረ ገጹን አድራሻ በአድራሻ መጻፊያው ውስጥ ይጻፉና Enter ይጫኑ። ወደ ቀድሞው ገጽ ለመመለስ የመመለሻ አዝራሩን ይጠቀሙ። ትር ከአንድ በላይ ገጽ ክፍት እንዲቆይ ያደርጋል።

title: Keeping your password safe
content: Use a long, unique password for each account. Do not share passwords or verification codes with anyone. A password manager can help you remember unique passwords. Turn on two-factor authentication when available.

title: የይለፍ ቃልዎን ይጠብቁ
content: ለእያንዳንዱ መለያ ረጅምና ልዩ የይለፍ ቃል ይጠቀሙ። የይለፍ ቃልዎን ወይም ማረጋገጫ ኮዶችን ለማንም አያጋሩ። የይለፍ ቃል አስተዳዳሪ ልዩ የይለፍ ቃሎችን ለማስታወስ ይረዳል። ሲኖር ባለሁለት ደረጃ ማረጋገጫን ያብሩ።

title: Sending your first email
content: Open your email application and choose Compose. Enter the recipient’s email address, add a clear subject, and write your message. Review the recipient and message before selecting Send. Never open an attachment from an unknown sender.

title: የመጀመሪያ ኢሜይልዎን መላክ
content: የኢሜይል መተግበሪያዎን ይክፈቱና አዲስ መልዕክት ይምረጡ። የተቀባዩን ኢሜይል አድራሻ ያስገቡ፣ ግልጽ ርዕስ ይጻፉ እና መልዕክትዎን ያዘጋጁ። ከመላክዎ በፊት ተቀባዩንና መልዕክቱን ያረጋግጡ። ከማያውቁት ላኪ የመጣ አባሪ አይክፈቱ።

title: Learning with a limited connection
content: Open a lesson while connected to save its text in this browser. When the connection drops, MELA can search saved public lesson content. The host page must already be open; first-time offline visits are not supported. Tutor messages, cloud AI, voice services, and screen sharing may require a connection.

title: በዝቅተኛ ግንኙነት መማር
content: የትምህርቱን ጽሑፍ በዚህ አሳሽ ለማስቀመጥ ከበይነመረብ ጋር ተገናኝተው ትምህርቱን ይክፈቱ። ግንኙነቱ ሲቋረጥ መላ የተቀመጠውን ጽሑፍ መፈለግ ይችላል። ገጹ አስቀድሞ ክፍት መሆን አለበት። የአስተማሪ መልዕክቶችና ማያ ገጽ ማጋራት ግንኙነት ይፈልጋሉ።

title: Offline-First & Localized AI
content: TRAINING SESSION · AI ENGINEERING How to build AI that works anywhere, in any language. No internet. No problem. Kidus Yohannes · Senior ML Engineer Our languages?

title: When the internet says no
content: Raise your hand if you have ever wanted to use AI, but the internet said no. Too slow. Too expensive. No signal at all.

title: 4 reasons AI must work offline
content: Connectivity: slow, costly or missing internet outside big cities. Privacy: health and student data never has to leave the device. Cost: every cloud AI request costs money and mobile data. Speed: no trip to a far-away server; instant answers.

title: Offline-first = a generator for your app
content: The power cuts. The generator starts. The lights stay on. Offline: everything important still works. Core features work. For AI this means the model runs locally. Online: sync, updates, bigger models. Connection adds bonus features and extras.

title: Where should the AI run?
content: A — Cloud: a huge remote server. Most powerful, but needs internet, charges per use, and data leaves the device. B — Local: on the user’s device. Works offline, private and free per use, but models are smaller and limited by the device. C — Hybrid: local first, cloud when online. Best of both, with more to design and test. Our pick for most projects: C, Hybrid, with local as the default.

title: Small models, big possibilities
content: Model size is measured in parameters: the numbers inside a model. Big cloud models: hundreds of billions. Laptop-size models: about 8 billion. Phone-size models: about 1–3 billion. Text and chat: Gemma, Llama, Phi, Qwen. Speech: Whisper for speech-to-text. Translation: NLLB, about 200 languages. Images: small vision models. Always check each model’s licence before building a product on it.

title: Quantization = compressing a photo
content: Same picture. Much smaller file. Original full-precision numbers are the 100% baseline. Quantize to 4-bit: look for Q4 or 4-bit labels; up to about 8× smaller. Pick the smallest model that does the job. Distil: a big teacher trains a small student. Focus on one job: focused beats general.

title: Pick your stage
content: Phone: LiteRT, Core ML, ONNX Runtime, MediaPipe. Great fit for field apps. Laptop: Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio. Great fit for staff tools and demos. Browser: WebGPU, Transformers.js, WebLLM. Nothing to install. Local server: one machine on local Wi-Fi can serve a whole school or clinic. Optional live demo: AI running with Wi-Fi off.

title: Myth vs fact
content: Myth: AI always needs the internet. Fact: small models run fully offline on laptops and phones. Myth: local AI is useless. Fact: for one focused task, a small model is often good enough. Myth: fine-tuning needs millions of examples. Fact: with LoRA, hundreds to a few thousand good examples can help.

title: Integrating an AI model in 5 steps
content: 1. Define the task. 2. Pick a model. 3. Test with real data. 4. Shrink and package. 5. One interface. The secret is step 5: your app asks “summarise this” and never cares which model answers. Like a phone charging socket: plug in any charger.

title: One socket, swappable engines
content: Your app connects to an AI layer or router. Online and allowed? Use cloud. Otherwise, use local. The local model is always available; the cloud model is optional when online. Sync queue: save on the device first, upload when the connection returns.

title: Does AI speak our language?
content: Most AI learned mostly from English. Amharic, Afaan Oromo and Tigrinya have far less training data. Illustrative tokenization: “hello” can be one piece; “ሰላም” can be split into more pieces. Ge’ez script may require more tokens, making processing slower, less accurate or costlier. More pieces mean more work for the model. Localization is not just translation. “Buying apples at Walmart for $3” in perfect Amharic is still strange. Use local names, places, money and examples.

title: 3 ways to make AI local
content: Easy — Go multilingual: start from models trained on many languages and test several. Medium — Open-book exam (RAG): the model looks up your documents, such as a curriculum or health guides, before answering. This can work offline. Advanced — Fine-tune (LoRA): teach a small model with local examples using a cheap add-on instead of a full retrain. Golden rule: test with native speakers. No score replaces a real human.

title: Reality check
content: Device limits: test on the cheapest phone your users own, not yours. Quality: keep a test set of real local examples; native speakers review. Model updates: download big models on Wi-Fi only and version every model. Licences and safety: check licences and tell users AI can be wrong.

title: Quiz time!
content: 1. What makes a model up to about 8× smaller, like compressing a photo? 2. What is the “open-book exam” technique called? 3. In a hybrid app, which model is the default?

title: And the answers are…
content: 1. Quantization. 2. RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation. 3. The local model.

title: What would you build first?
content: Offline tutor: answers students’ questions in their own language, with no internet. Clinic assistant: speak notes in the local language and turn them into an organised record. Farmer helper: a photo of a sick plant leads to a likely disease and advice. Voice access: speech-to-text for people who prefer speaking. Shout out your idea!

title: 4 things to remember
content: 1. Design for no internet; connection is a bonus. 2. Small, quantized models run on phones, laptops and local servers. 3. One interface: swap local and cloud models freely. 4. Localize: multilingual models, local knowledge and native speakers. Questions? Kidus Yohannes · Senior ML Engineer.
